messages:
Sam W: Running a quick post-merge perf sweep — saw a ~18% p99 hop on 8-GPU TP+PP jobs after the remat change. Not huge but repeatable across two clusters.
Jia L: ugh, which remat change? the one that shifted remat points to layer boundaries?
Sam W: Yes, remat points moved to module boundaries to simplify gradients. Perf profile looks like all-reduce waits spiking during backward recompute windows.
Marco R: Can you paste the flame or nvprof sample? Even a tiny scheduling wobble can amplify all-reduce stalls on our interconnect.
Sam W: Paste of the short profile dump (top 6 lines):
```
BackwardStep1 (recompute): compute 6.2ms | wait_allreduce 4.7ms
KVCacheRestore: compute 0.9ms | wait_allreduce 2.1ms
BackwardStep2: compute 5.8ms | wait_allreduce 6.3ms
AllReduce(A): 2.0ms | kernel 1.3ms
AllReduce(B): 3.1ms | kernel 2.0ms
Total step: 40.6ms
```
Sam W: The weird bit is the KV cache restore overlaps partially but then recompute waves cause meta-synchronization and amplify allreduce latency.
Elaine P: Did kernel selection change on the release? I remember we toggled the NCCL algorithm or kernel for small reductions.
Jia L: We did introduce a kernel fallback for quantized matmuls around the same CL, but that shouldn't touch allreduce. However the batching heuristics were adjusted to prefer slightly larger batches (to reduce kernel churn).
Marco R: Larger micro-batches + remat can create longer compute tails and narrower windows for effective overlap. If all ranks hit the recompute barrier at similar times -> allreduce queueing.
Sam W: I instrumented per-rank step skew — variance went from 0.9ms -> 3.7ms after the change. That correlates with the allreduce stall.
Elaine P: Can we try forcing the old remat points + new batching? Or flip batching heuristics back to previous heuristic (prefer more small batches) just to isolate cause.
Sam W: I ran two quick experiments: (A) old remat + new batching -> no regression. (B) new remat + old batching -> still regressed but smaller (~6%). So remat looks like primary culprit.
Jia L: Good catch. Could be that remat increased peak concurrent reductions because recompute pushes more threads into collective at once.
Marco R: For a quick mitigation, we could: 1) add jitter to remat start offsets across TP ranks, 2) change kernel selection to prioritize asynchronous allreduce-friendly kernels, or 3) tweak batching to create staggered micro-batches.
Sam W: I prototyped (1) jitter with a per-rank seed delta of 200-800us — p99 improved ~9% but mean unaffected. Still exploring correctness edge cases.
Elaine P: Option (2) requires validation: some NCCL algorithms have better tail latency in our topology. Might be a kernel selector flag we can toggle per-model.
perf-bot: Perf regression detected: job redwood/serving/exp-pp-tp-43 — p99 increased by 18% at 1767894200. Auto-created issue #INF-1218.
Jia L: Let's avoid rollout for the remat change until we decide. Can we gate it behind a config flag per-deployment?
Sam W: I'll push a hotfix that keeps previous remat layout behind a feature flag and add the jitter experiment as an opt-in.
Marco R: Also add a quick profiling hook to log per-callstack allreduce timestamps so we can see which operator sequences cause the worst spikes. Even a compact CSV is fine.
Sam W: Will do. Plan: (a) revert default remat placement behind flag, (b) land per-rank jitter opt-in, (c) add allreduce timestamp tracing and kernel-selection toggle for canary. Targeting canary tomorrow.
Elaine P: Sounds good. If canary looks stable we can test kernel selector permutations on the Dedicated pool (lower blast radius).
Sam W: Thanks — will post results in this thread. @deploy-bot please block rollout of remat-change to prod until further notice.
deploy-bot: Rollout blocked for change `remat-points-v2` (block reason: perf-investigation).
